papers.title: On do Carmo's Question: The Properly Embedded Case
papers.summary: In this paper, we prove that every complete noncompact two-sided properly embedded constant mean curvature hypersurface of finite Morse index in Euclidean space is minimal. The result holds in every dimension. We assume no bounds on curvature or volume growth. This establishes the properly embedded case of the finite-index version of do Carmo's question. For nonzero mean curvature, we use the radii of inscribed balls to define a positive weight. This weight gives a polynomial bound on weighted volume, while its reciprocal satisfies a differential inequality involving the Jacobi operator. We combine these properties with stability outside a compact set to obtain finite total area. This leads to a contradiction.

papers.title: On the elliptic regularization of maximal slope curves
papers.summary: We consider the so-called Weighted Energy-Dissipation approximation of gradient flows in metric spaces. We prove the convergence of minimizers to maximal slope curves under assumptions that are close to those of the original existence theory for metric gradient flows. The proof relies on an energy-dissipation identity for the approximating curves and on an adaptation of a general stability result for maximal slope curves.

papers.title: The isoperimetric problem in the Riemannian Heisenberg $3$-space
papers.summary: We prove that every closed weakly stable constant mean curvature surface immersed in the Riemannian Heisenberg space ${\rm Nil}_3$ is an embedded rotational sphere. As a consequence, we solve the isoperimetric problem in ${\rm Nil}_3$: the isoperimetric domains of ${\rm Nil}_3$ are exactly the regions enclosed by rotational constant mean curvature spheres, and for each prescribed volume there is a unique such domain, up to ambient isometry. For small volumes, the isoperimetric result was proved by Tomter in 1993.

papers.title: Gradient higher integrability for a general class of degenerate parabolic double phase systems
papers.summary: We establish quantitative local higher integrability estimates for weak solutions of degenerate parabolic systems with generalized double phase growth, whose prototype is $$u_t-\operatorname{div}\left(\frac{G'(|Du|)}{|Du|}Du+a(x,t)\frac{H'(|Du|)}{|Du|}Du\right)=0\qquad\text{in }Ω_T.$$ Here $G$ and $H$ are Young functions satisfying suitable structural assumptions. The nonnegative coefficient $a$ is allowed to vanish and has a concave modulus of continuity $ω$ with respect to the parabolic distance. For $Ψ(z,\varkappa)=G(\varkappa)+a(z)H(\varkappa)$, we prove that solutions in $L^\infty(0,T;L^s(Ω,\mathbb{R}^N))$, $2\le s<\infty$, satisfy $Ψ(\cdot,|Du|)\in L^{1+\varepsilon}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ for some $\varepsilon>0$, provided $$\limsup_{ρ\to 0+}ω(ρ)\frac{H(ρ^{-\frac{n+s}{s}})}{G(ρ^{-\frac{n+s}{s}})}<\infty.$$ For bounded solutions, the corresponding condition involves $H(ρ^{-1})/G(ρ^{-1})$. These conditions extend the known interpolative gap bounds from power growth to general growth functions and continuity moduli. In particular, for $G(\varkappa)=\varkappa^p$, $H(\varkappa)=\varkappa^q$, and $ω(ρ)\simeqρ^α$, they recover $q\le p+sα/(n+s)$ and $q\le p+α$, respectively. The proof combines an intrinsic stopping-time argument with inverse-function estimates to derive Poincaré and reverse Hölder inequalities adapted to the general growth phases.

papers.title: Shock solutions of a 3D spherical piston problem for the compressible Euler equations
papers.summary: This paper establishes the global well-posedness of shock solutions for a 3D spherical piston problem to the compressible Euler equations. The main mathematical challenges are the nonlinear coupling between the free shock boundary and the moving piston, alongside potential gradient catastrophes induced by spherical geometric source terms. To overcome these difficulties, we reformulate the problem using Riemann invariants and introduce a tailored directional derivative along the unperturbed piston trajectory. Then we can extend the local solution to construct a global piecewise smooth solution including a single shock under some moderate assumptions.

papers.title: Uniqueness of Extremizers and Convergence of the Euler-Lagrange Iteration for the Critical Hardy-Littlewood-Sobolev Inequality
papers.summary: Let $n \ge 3$, $2 \le α< n$, and $1 < p,r < \infty$ satisfy $p^{-1}+r^{-1}=1+α/n$. We prove uniqueness, up to common translations and dilations, of the normalized nonnegative extremizing pairs for the corresponding Hardy-Littlewood-Sobolev inequality. More generally, all positive finite-energy solutions of the Euler-Lagrange system belong to a single symmetry orbit. The proof compares two solutions at different relative scales. Total positivity of order two identifies the second eigenspace of an associated compact self-adjoint operator and forces each nonzero difference to change sign exactly once. The opposite orientations obtained at the two ends of the scale parameter then yield uniqueness. The same method proves radial nondegeneracy modulo dilation. We also establish strong convergence of the normalized alternating Euler-Lagrange iteration from every nonnegative, radially nonincreasing initial datum to a fixed extremizing pair, without rescaling the iterates. Square-root mass variables reduce the exclusion of several concentration profiles to a static spectral estimate and an energy-increment argument. The analysis includes sublinear exponents and the logarithmic borderline decay regimes.

papers.title: Viscosity-variational inequality solutions of fully nonlinear second-order stationary mean field games with nonseparable and nondifferentiable Hamiltonians
papers.summary: We analyse stationary fully nonlinear uniformly elliptic second-order mean field games with nonseparable and nondifferentiable Hamiltonians by introducing the notion of viscosity-variational inequality solution. In this formulation of the problem, the value function is the viscosity solution of the Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman (HJB) equation, and the Kolmogorov--Fokker--Planck (KFP) equation for the player density is understood as a nonstandard variational inequality that no longer involves partial derivatives of the value function. The advantages of this formulation are found in its stability and continuity properties for handling weak convergence arguments, which we use to prove the existence of solutions of the problem. Furthermore, we prove the equivalence of the notion of viscosity-variational inequality solution with the notion of a partial differential inclusion solution, where the value function is a strong solution of the HJB equation and the player density is a very weak solution of the KFP equation with coefficients belonging to subdifferential sets of the Hamiltonian. Finally, we prove the uniqueness of solutions in the case of separable Hamiltonians with strictly monotone couplings.

papers.title: Failure of Pólya-Szegő inequality for weighted nonlocal seminorm and on nonlocal C-K-N inequality
papers.summary: We create counterexamples to show that Pólya-Szegő type of inequality fails for the weighted nonlocal seminorm \begin{equation*} [u]_{W^{s,p, α}(\mathbb{R}^d)} := \left( \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \frac{|x|^{α_{1} p} |y|^{α_{2} p} |u(x)-u(y)|^{p}}{|x-y|^{d+sp}} \, dx \, dy \right)^{\frac{1}{p}} \ , \end{equation*} in all three regimes $α_1 +α_2 < 0, \, α_1 +α_2 = 0$, and $α_1 +α_2 >0$. These counterexamples are such that it completely settles the first two cases for all parameters. We also provide necessary and sufficient conditions on the parameters for $ [u]_{W^{s,p, α}(\mathbb{R}^d)} < \infty$, thus extending an earlier known result of [Serena Dipierro and Enrico Valdinoci, A density property for fractional weighted Sobolev spaces]. We also provide another proof of the fractional C-K-N type inequality, for most of the parameters (Hardy and Sobolev are included), using a familiar technique which is involved in the proof of fractional Sobolev inequality of [Eleonora Di Nezza, Giampiero Palatucci, and Enrico Valdinoci, Hitchhiker's guide to the fractional Sobolev spaces, Bulletin des sciences mathematiques] together with a symmetrization technique.

papers.title: Gradient potential estimates for k-Hessian equations
papers.summary: For $2\le k<n$, we prove pointwise gradient bounds for proper weak $k$-convex functions in terms of a local average and a Wolff potential of the full Hessian measure $F_k[u]$. The estimate yields local Lipschitz regularity for $F_k[u]=f$ with $f\in L^{n/k,1/k}_{\mathrm{loc}}$, and for $F_k[u]=|Du|^p$ when $0<p<nk/(n-k)$. Both the Lorentz index $1/k$ and the upper bound on $p$ are sharp.

papers.title: Non-Isothermal Plane Couette Flow for the Boltzmann Equation in Three Dimensions
papers.summary: We study the Boltzmann equation for a non-isothermal plane Couette flow in the three-dimensional channel $\mathbb T_x\times(-1,1)_y\times\mathbb T_z$ for Maxwell molecules. For sufficiently small shear rate and wall temperature perturbations, we construct a unique steady solution near the global Maxwellian. For the corresponding unsteady boundary value problem, we establish the global existence and uniqueness of solutions arising from small perturbations of the steady state, together with their exponential convergence to the steady state as $t\to\infty$. A major difficulty in both the steady and unsteady problems is to close the outgoing mass fluxes generated by diffuse reflection. To overcome this difficulty, we develop a new boundary flux transmission framework which, in the slab geometry, yields steady and time-dependent wall flux estimates through the boundary-to-boundary transmission between the two walls. We further extend this framework to damped transport equations with diffuse reflection in general bounded $C^1$ domains, even when the damping coefficient degenerates at large velocities.

papers.title: Uniqueness and nondegeneracy for a critical Choquard equation with Hardy potential
papers.summary: We study the critical Choquard equation \[ -Δu-μ|x|^{-2}u =\bigl(|\cdot|^{2-N}*|u|^p\bigr)|u|^{p-2}u \qquad\text{in }\mathbb R^N, \] where $|\cdot|^{2-N}$ is the Newton kernel, $p=\frac{N+2}{N-2}$, and $0<μ<\frac{(N-2)^2}{4}$. For every $N\ge3$, we prove that positive solutions in $D^{1,2}(\mathbb R^N)$ are radially symmetric about the origin, unique up to dilation, and nondegenerate. Our proof uses normalized logarithmic derivatives to obtain a cooperative system. The resulting monotonicity principle underlies both the uniqueness and nondegeneracy arguments, and remains effective in the subquadratic range $1<p<2$, corresponding to $N\ge7$. Consequently, the linearized quadratic form has Morse index one and the sharp inequality admits a global quadratic remainder estimate. The best constant is strictly concave in the Hardy parameter on $\bigl[0,\frac{(N-2)^2}{4}\bigr)$, is of class $C^2$ with strictly negative second derivative in the interior, and satisfies two-sided bounds that agree to first order at $μ=0$.

papers.title: The Short Pulse equation on the half lines: a Riemann--Hilbert approach
papers.summary: In this work, we analyze the initial boundary value (IBV) problems for the Short Pulse (SP) equation $u_{xt}=u+\frac{1}{6}(u^3)_{xx}$ (classical solutions) on the half-lines $x\ge 0$ and $x\le 0$ under the condition of sufficient decay as $x\to +\infty$ or as $x\to -\infty$. Using the Riemann--Hilbert (RH) problem approach, we show that these two IBV problems differ substantially regarding the boundary values required for problems to be well-posed. Namely, the solution of the ``right problem'' ($x\ge 0$) is uniquely determined by the initial data $u(x,0)$, $x\ge 0$ alone, whereas for the ``left problem'' ($x\le 0$), two boundary functions $u(0,t)$ and $u_x(0,t)$ have to be prescribed, together with the initial data, for a well-posed problem.

papers.title: The stochastic Ginzburg-Landau equation with harmonic potential in the full subcritical regime
papers.summary: In this paper, we construct the complex Ginzburg-Landau dynamic associated with the harmonic oscillator, with a random force which is white in time and covers the full subcritical range in space. We are able to renormalise the non-linearity using the same constant as the one used to renormalise the problem associated to the Laplacian. By an extension of the problem to complex times, we are able to prove that the solution of the complex Ginzburg-Landau is equal in law to the solution of the purely dissipative case, i.e. the associated complex $Φ^4$ model, but along a complex axis of time.

papers.title: Hypocoercivity for a thermostatted Boltzmann equation
papers.summary: We study the Boltzmann equation for a gas on the three-dimensional torus. Its particles collide with one another and with a thermal reservoir whose temperature varies in space. The reservoir heats the gas in some regions and cools it in others, driving a nonequilibrium energy current. For the isotropic cutoff kernel, with Maxwell molecules or hard potentials, we prove global well-posedness and exponential convergence to the same stationary state for initial data with a common Gaussian upper bound and Gaussian moment bound. These bounds determine how weak self collisions must be relative to bath collisions. The estimates are uniform over bath profiles between fixed positive temperature bounds. For any nonconstant reservoir profile on the three-dimensional torus, this stationary state cannot be a local Maxwellian. When particles collide only with the bath, relative entropy to the stationary state cannot increase. Once self collisions are added, arbitrarily small perturbations can initially increase it, even though they later return exponentially.

papers.title: Multiplicity via symmetry for the Minkowski mean curvature equation: Dirichlet and Neumann problems
papers.summary: We consider the Minkowski mean curvature equation $$ -\operatorname{div}\left(\frac{\nabla u}{\sqrt{1-|\nabla u|^2}}\right) =λu+μh(x,u) \quad \text{in } Ω, \quad \mathcal B u = 0 \quad \text{on } \partial Ω, $$ where $\mathcal B \in \{ \mathcal D, \mathcal N \}$ is a Dirichlet or Neumann boundary condition and $Ω$ is a smooth bounded domain, required to be convex in the Neumann case. Moreover, $λ, μ\geq0$ are parameters, and $h(x,u)$ is odd with respect to $u$ and positive for $u > 0$. Using minmax methods in nonsmooth critical point theory, we prove that $λ>λ^\mathcal B_k$ yields at least $k$ pairs of nontrivial solutions with negative energy for every $μ\geq0$, where $λ_k^\mathcal B$ are the corresponding Laplacian eigenvalues, indexed by $λ^\mathcal B_0=0$. Moreover, if $H(x,u):=\int_0^u h(x,t)\,dt=o(u^2)$ as $u\to0$, we prove that for $λ\in[λ^\mathcal B_k,λ^\mathcal B_{k+1})$ and every $j\geq\max\{1,k\}$, sufficiently large $μ$ yields at least $2j-k$ distinct pairs of solutions: $j$ with negative energy and $j-k$ with positive energy.

papers.title: Log-concavity and level set curvature estimates for the first Dirichlet eigenfunction in hyperbolic space
papers.summary: In this paper, we study the first Dirichlet eigenfunction on bounded, smooth and strictly horo-convex domains in hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^n$. We prove its strict $\log$-concavity in arbitrary dimension and establish the Gauss curvature bound $K>1$ for its level sets. In dimensions two and three, we further obtain quantitative lower bounds for $K$ in terms of the minimum Gauss curvature of the boundary. In higher dimensions, the product of the two smallest principal curvatures of each level hypersurface exceeds one. Furthermore, we extend the strict $\log$-concavity result to bounded smooth horo-convex domains. Our approach combines maximum or minimum principles for suitable auxiliary functions, boundary convexity estimates and a domain deformation argument.

papers.title: Global Solvability in Critical Sobolev Spaces for divergence-type equations associated with elliptic systems of vector fields
papers.summary: In this work, we present global solvability results, in critical Sobolev spaces, for divergence-type equations associated with elliptic systems of vector fields.

papers.title: A Feynman-Kac Representation and Large Deviation Bounds for the Fisher-KPP Equation Driven by Finite-Activity Pure Jump Noise
papers.summary: We study the asymptotic propagation speed of travelling wave solutions to the stochastic Fisher-KPP equation with multiplicative finite-activity pure jump Lévy noise. The noise is represented by a compensated Poisson random measure with finite intensity, so that the solution evolves deterministically between successive jump times and undergoes multiplicative jumps at the event times. Our main contribution is a stochastic Feynman-Kac representation for the solution, which expresses the random field as the product of the exponential martingale of the jump noise and an expectation over the paths of an independent Brownian motion. This representation is the key probabilistic tool that converts the nonlinear stochastic partial differential equation into an expectation problem, thereby allowing for a direct analysis of the front position. Building on this representation and on the large deviation analysis of the jump noise, we derive explicit upper and lower bounds for the asymptotic wave speed. These bounds are given in terms of the noise intensity $ε$ and the Lévy measure $μ$, providing a quantitative description of how discontinuous stochastic forcing affects the propagation speed in the Fisher-KPP equation. Under the finite-activity assumption, a stopping-time iteration yields pathwise $L^\infty$ bounds and finite-speed propagation of the level sets of the front, which are essential for establishing the existence of a travelling wave profile. The framework extends naturally to multi-species cooperative systems, illustrating its robustness. Numerical simulations are included to demonstrate the informativeness of the theoretical speed bounds.

papers.title: Liouville systems I: Blow-up analysis and orthogonal decomposition
papers.summary: We study blow-up solutions of generalized Liouville systems on a closed surface at and near critical parameter hypersurfaces. Under a Morse assumption on the reduced functional, we establish the following results. First, we introduce amplitude variables in the approximate manifold and prove that every sequence of blow-up solutions at a fixed critical parameter, or along an admissible sequence from the lower side, admits a unique minimizing decomposition up to permutation. The remainder converges to zero and is orthogonal to the center, scale, and amplitude directions. The concentration scales are comparable, the limiting configuration satisfies the scale balance conditions, and the amplitudes vanish after multiplication by the logarithmic scale. Second, we determine the leading parameter defect in both critical decay regimes and prove that, along each fixed admissible path, all sufficiently large solutions lie in finitely many disjoint bubbling neighborhoods. Finally, assuming the leading coefficient is nonzero at every balanced critical configuration, the solution set at the fixed critical parameter is compact. These results provide the analytic foundation for studying the resonant degree via critical points at infinity.

papers.title: Quantifying and minimizing collision intensity in stationary crowd flow
papers.summary: We develop a continuum model to quantify kinematic collision risk in stationary crowd flow. From the density-weighted inward relative flux, we derive a collision functional based on the symmetric velocity gradient. For incompressible flows with constant density, this functional is convex and positively homogeneous of degree one in a combination of second derivatives of the stream function. We minimize it subject to prescribed boundary flux. On bounded simply connected domains with Lipschitz boundary, under a finite-energy lifting assumption, we prove existence of minimizers in a relaxed class that allows this derivative combination to be a vector-valued Radon measure. We show that disks are the only domains with a nontrivial zero-trace kernel, corresponding to rigid rotation about the center. Using the compact embedding for functions of bounded deformation, we prove that relaxed energy sublevels are compact without normalization on every other admissible domain, and after removing one rotational component on disks. We identify the relaxed functional with the strong $W^{1,1}$ lower semicontinuous envelope of the functional on the prescribed-trace class with integrable controlled derivatives. Then, we derive optimality conditions via convex duality. We construct explicit radial flows on annular sectors and prove that they minimize the energy over the full admissible classes, including nonradial competitors. On the square, distinct minimizers with the same prescribed boundary flux have different local collision intensities. The square--disk comparison shows that the saddle flow loses optimality when the domain changes, even after normalization.

papers.title: A Lagrangian Approach to Uniqueness for Active Scalars in Generalized Mean Oscillation Spaces
papers.summary: We develop a unified Lagrangian framework for the uniqueness of weak solutions to a broad class of two-dimensional inviscid active scalar equations in generalized mean oscillation spaces. Under common structural assumptions on the Biot--Savart kernels, we identify mean oscillation spaces that ensure an Osgood condition for the velocity, and establish uniqueness in these classes. For the two-dimensional Euler equations, we establish uniqueness for vorticities whose mean oscillation grows mildly at small scales, extending beyond $\mathrm{BMO}$. For the surface quasi-geostrophic (SQG) and incompressible porous media (IPM) equations, we obtain uniqueness in spaces logarithmically rougher than $C^{0,1}$. We also obtain what are (to our knowledge) the strongest known uniqueness results for the $α$-SQG equation, $0<α<1$, in spaces logarithmically rougher than critical Hölder spaces $C^α$. The framework also applies to various logarithmically perturbed models, yielding uniqueness in the corresponding sharp regularity classes. The proof combines a sharp regularity estimate for the velocity with a stability estimate for integral operators under measure-preserving rearrangements. This provides a single uniqueness argument for the entire family under common structural assumptions on the kernels.

papers.title: Singular viscosity-exponent limit for one-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes equations with far field vacuum
papers.summary: We consider the limit $δ\to1^+$ for the one-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes equations with viscosity $μ(ρ)=ρ^δ$ and far field vacuum. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first result on the viscosity-exponent limit $δ\to1^+$ for strong solutions with far field vacuum. With far field vacuum, the diffusion coefficient $ρ^{δ-1}$ does not converge uniformly to $1$ on $\mathbb R$ as $δ\to1^+$. The main difficulty is to obtain uniform estimates for this limit. By introducing some new weighted density variables, we establish local well-posedness and uniform estimates without requiring $ρ_0^{(δ-1)/2}\in L^2(\mathbb R)$. We prove strong convergence to the known global $δ=1$ solution obtained in \cite{WenZhangDCDS2025} on a local time interval independent of $δ$. With one additional order of regularity of the initial data and the limit solution, the convergence holds on every fixed finite time interval, and the maximal life-spans of the $δ>1$ solutions tend to $+\infty$ as $δ\to1^+$.

papers.title: Instability of Self-Similar Implosions for the Compressible Euler Equations
papers.summary: We prove that all known regular self-similar implosion solutions of the isentropic compressible Euler equations are unstable to shock formation. The perturbations can be chosen to be small in a class determined by the regularity threshold of the background. The proof relies on an amplification mechanism which occurs along the surface of the backward sonic cone from the implosion point. Motivated by our main results, we formulate an implosion censorship conjecture for the compressible Euler equations, stating that classical implosions are unstable to shock formation.

papers.title: Second-order geometric consistency of nonlinear FE-HMM on surfaces via corrector non-degeneracy
papers.summary: We analyze the geometric variational crime of nonlinear finite element heterogeneous multiscale methods (FE--HMM) for $p$-growth monotone laws on curved surfaces, $p\ge2$. The practical method projects discrete gradients onto the exact tangent planes; we compare it with the exactly lifted method on the same discrete space. Without further hypotheses, the difference is $O(h_g^{p/(p-1)})$ in the metric induced by the cell correctors. The optimal order $O(h_g^2)$ holds with a constant given by a weighted negative moment of the corrected gradients, evaluated along the practical solution only; no bounds on discrete gradients in $L^\infty$ are used. The negative moment is a sufficient condition for the lower shifted $p$-structure of the discrete homogenized flux, which for $p>2$ is not available in general. For the model law and a fixed cell mesh, its uniform boundedness is equivalent to a finite-dimensional directional criterion on degenerate correctors, and for laminates it holds with an explicit bound, uniform in the cell mesh. With macro--micro quasi-optimality and an estimate for coefficient sampling, the reconstructed microscopic field converges as $O(h+H^{\min{s,1}}+h_g^2)$, where $H^s$ is the cell approximation rate. Experiments on a torus with an exact closest-point lift and a transported anisotropic $p=4$ material show second-order geometric convergence up to $98,304$ macroscopic quadrature points, each with a fully solved nonlinear cell problem, with bounded a posteriori constants for both load treatments.

papers.title: Global well-posedness for the energy-critical focusing NLS on $\mathbb T^3$
papers.summary: We prove global well-posedness for the focusing quintic nonlinear Schrödinger equation on the standard three-dimensional torus for initial data below the mass-corrected energy and Sobolev-norm thresholds determined by the Euclidean ground state. This gives a subthreshold focusing counterpart to the defocusing theorem of Ionescu and Pausader. The proof combines the periodic profile analysis with the recent nonradial Euclidean scattering theorem of Su and Zhao. The mass correction yields an invariant region and a nonnegative energy decomposition, placing every Euclidean profile below both ground-state thresholds. Uniform bounds on finite intervals follow from a contradiction argument on shrinking time intervals.
